facts.text: Gardners takes its name from Uriah Gardner, a local miller who built the first feed mill and post office in the late 1800s.
The town’s birth came with the railroad: the Reading Company bought the line in 1891, and Gardners Station opened in 1912 for passengers and freight.
In 1912 Musselman built a second processing plant in Gardners, beginning apple processing the following fall and expanding the local fruit industry.
During World War I, the Gardners and Biglerville plants kept canned fruit flowing despite labor, fuel, and transportation shortages.
Today Knouse Foods keeps a warehouse in Gardners, producing over 300 products that ship to more than 50 countries worldwide.
Gardners sits just off Pennsylvania Route 34 in Tyrone Township, surrounded by apple orchards that have defined the region’s agriculture.
